correctness.rationale: PASS. For any complex two-plane F of 3x3 matrices, determinant det(sA+tB) is a homogeneous cubic on CP1, hence has a projective root (or vanishes identically). This yields a nonzero rank≤2 matrix, with Schatten ratio ≥2^(1/q-1/p) for 0<p<q≤infty. In the explicit complex plane span{I,diag(1,ζ,ζ²)}, singular values |a+bζ^j| satisfy the exact equilateral linear relation and all triangle inequalities for arbitrary COMPLEX a,b. For 0<p≤1, p-power subadditivity caps each normalized w_j=s_j^p/Σs^p at 1/2; convexity of t^(q/p) on the capped simplex yields norm ratio ≤2^(1/q-1/p), with q=infty from the same cap. I-U has singular values (0,√3,√3) and achieves equality. A one-dimensional identity subspace gives c9=3^(1/q-1/p). Proof depends essentially on algebraically closed complex field and on p≤1; supplementary finite coefficients cannot replace the universal inequality.
